Subject: Data locality constraints & hosting mode next steps — EmberHealth

Hi Lena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment on hosting mode implications (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Call highlights:
- Compliance: EmberHealth confirmed EU-only processing for PHI and patient-identifiable datasets for now; APAC presence is "possible later this year" but not required for the initial rollout.
- Workload profile: expected peak inference load ~120 requests/sec (90% sub-1s latency target), mostly short text prompts (avg 150 tokens).
- Retention & audit: 30–90 day retention window for logs, SOC 2 + willingness to provide additional attestation evidence.

Hosting mode implications we discussed:
- Hosted API (EU region): Fastest onboarding (1–2 weeks), supports region-scoped hosting in EU, Redwood-managed keys. Cross-region fallback (if EU capacity is constrained) will still route to EU-preferring pools first; we can configure strict no-egress to non-EU if required (but that adds operational gating).
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): Predictable throughput and isolated capacity; deployment typically 4–6 weeks with reserved commit; good middle-ground for predictable SLAs without full VPC setup.
- Private VPC / on-prem: Strongest control for PHI/data locality; timeline ~8–10 weeks for initial setup (longer if air-gapped). Requires network & security coordination on your side (VPN/Direct Connect, firewall rules, KMS integration).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether any downstream systems require cross-border access to processed outputs (i.e., do any of your apps in APAC need live access to responses)? Answer determines whether strict EU-only routing is mandatory.
2) Please share a redacted data inventory or scope sheet (we discussed a high-level inventory) — I attached a template below.
3) If Private VPC is preferred, please nominate the technical point-of-contact for network kickoff (we'll loop Aditya).

Attachments: EmberDataRequirements_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — simple checklist to capture retention, egress, and PHI flags.

I'll follow up with cost/lead-time ballparks from Ben + a short matrix of tradeoffs. Thanks — Grace

--

Hi Lena — Ben here (solutions + pricing). Appreciate the inventory — that helps. Short technical and commercial notes so EmberHealth can evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: 

Hosted API (EU region):
- Timeline: 1–2 weeks for a scoped onboarding + contract.
- Controls: We can enforce EU-region tenancy for processed data and support customer-managed KMS for at-rest keys (additional paperwork). However, strict EU-only egress (no cross-region fallback) is possible but increases RTO for capacity spikes — we recommend a hard SLA + provisioned Dedicated if you need a hard no-egress guarantee.
- Ballpark cost: lowest up-front; pay-as-you-go. Good for quick pilot.

Dedicated capacity (EU-only):
- Timeline: typically 4–6 weeks from signed commitment.
- Benefits: dedicated GPU pool, capacity guarantees, predictable unit economics; supports transparent peering options.
- Ballpark cost: mid-range; commitment required (we'll provide ranges once we have expected peak QPS and retention).

Private VPC / on-prem: 
- Timeline: 8–10+ weeks depending on networking approvals and KMS/HSM integration.
- Benefits: full control over network egress, audit log residency, single-tenant runtime.
- Considerations: operational handoff + security review.

Questions for EmberHealth to finalize a recommendation:
1) Final peak QPS target (you mentioned ~120 rps) and expected steady-state.
2) Exact retention window for request logs/KV cache.
3) Any additional certification evidence needed beyond SOC2 (e.g., contractual language or DPA clauses specifying EU-only processing).

I attached a one-pager matrix comparing modes. If you want, we can sketch a recommended path: Hosted EU-region for a 6–8 week pilot with a parallel procurement review for Dedicated/EU Private depending on pilot results.

Attachments: hosting_modes_quickmatrix.pdf (pdf)
